name: Burgruine Vilsegg
kurzbeschreibung: The romantic castle ruin of Vilsegg crowns a rocky ridge near Vils in the Außerfern, offering sweeping vistas across the Tannheimer Tal and Allgäu alpine foothills.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Vilsegg Castle Ruins (Burgruine Vilsegg) rise dramatically upon a densely forested rocky crest northwest of the historic town of Vils in the Tyrolean Außerfern region, right along the border with Bavaria. Constructed in the 13th century by the Prince-Bishops of Augsburg as a mighty defensive stronghold to safeguard the frontier against the expanding Counts of Tyrol, Vilsegg stands as one of the oldest and most architecturally intriguing fortification sites in the Reutte district. Although abandoned to progressive decay from the 17th century onwards, the soaring medieval stone masonry continues to exude a romantic fascination that draws history enthusiasts and alpine hikers from all around.

Route & Requirements

From the historic town center of Vils, an exemplary signposted panoramic trail ascends gently through dense mixed mountain forests up to the sunny castle plateau. Upon arrival, hikers can explore the towering remnants of the historic keep, thick curtain walls, and excavated foundations of medieval residential chambers. Informative on-site display boards detail the fortress's eventful construction history, archaeological excavations, and the austere daily life of the medieval garrison. From protected stone vantage points, sweeping views unfold over the Allgäu Alps, the verdant Vils Valley, and rugged border ridges. The hike requires basic fitness and sturdy hiking boots with grippy soles, as damp forest paths can become slippery.

Visit & Arrival

The entire outdoor ruin area is freely accessible year-round at any time of day free of charge and at visitors' own discretion. During winter months, icy snow requires appropriate footwear and caution along the sloping paths. Public transit: take the Außerfernbahn railway from Reutte or Kempten directly to Vils in Tirol station; from there, it takes about thirty-five minutes on foot along the castle trail. Motorists travel via the B179 Fernpass road or from Füssen via the B16; free public parking is available in central Vils and near the local sports fields.

Tips

Combine your historical castle exploration with a leisurely stroll through the charming old town of Vils, recognized as one of the smallest chartered cities in Austria. An onward hike along the border trail toward the deep blue lake Alatsee or over to Füssen offers breathtaking views of the world-famous Neuschwanstein Castle close by.
preis: Freely accessible (viewing the castle ruin is free of charge)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round during daylight hours (sturdy footing required in snowy conditions)
